events.scenario_brief: A week before the Chicago conference, the airline moves Kara's Thursday outbound later by 35 minutes, still arriving within the presenter check-in window but leaving less slack before the connected hotel check-in and materials drop. The official hotel confirms the queen room and coffee maker, but the mini-fridge remains a request rather than a guarantee, and the presenter packet adds a separate Friday-morning room-access step before her panel. The Sunday afternoon return is unchanged, and the main loose pieces are the fridge request, seat assignments, and a compact plan for carrying lab materials without using rideshares.

events.continuity_hook: Starts the next clinic-training episode after the fall conference, with the schedule compact enough that return timing and dependable hotel basics matter more than sightseeing.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Tuesday outbound and Thursday return patterns, narrow the hotel shortlist around reviews and room amenities, decide whether to plan on a compact rental or rideshares, and prepare questions for the clinic about access, storage, and parking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Chicago conference, a pediatric rehab clinic in Raleigh asks Kara to come in for an October orthotics follow-up visit with a Tuesday evening staff demo, a full Wednesday training day, and Thursday morning coaching. Tampa flight options are workable, but the return choice is between a clean Thursday afternoon itinerary and a cheaper later connection that would get her home too late to feel useful on Friday. The clinic-adjacent hotel is convenient but has uneven recent reviews and unclear mini-fridge details, while a better-rated suite property farther out confirms queen rooms, coffee makers, mini-fridges, a fitness room, and an indoor pool but no hot tub. The unresolved pieces are storage for teaching materials, suburban transportation, and whether the extra hotel distance is worth the more reliable room setup.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Raleigh clinic visit from comparison into booking once the host clarifies access, storage, and the Thursday finish.
events.interaction_goal: Book the Tuesday outbound and Thursday afternoon return if the fare still holds, reserve the cancellable suite hotel, add the compact rental, and select window seats where the seat map allows.
events.scenario_brief: The Raleigh clinic confirms Tuesday evening badge pickup, a locked office for Kara's equipment, and Thursday wrap-up by 12:30 p.m. The best itinerary now uses a Tuesday late-morning Tampa departure and a Thursday afternoon return with enough time to get from the clinic to the airport without rushing. The suite hotel remains the stronger fit because it has better reviews, a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool, while the clinic-adjacent hotel still cannot confirm the fridge. A compact rental looks more dependable than rideshares because the hotel, clinic, and grocery stop are spread across different parts of the suburb.

events.continuity_hook: Tightens the Raleigh trip after booking, with the practical focus shifting to airport timing, construction parking, and keeping the final clinic morning realistic.
events.interaction_goal: Choose between the earlier revised return and the later safer option, recheck seat assignments, map the temporary clinic parking route, and set Thursday checkout and airport departure timing.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Raleigh visit, the airline moves Kara's Thursday return 50 minutes earlier, making the clinic-to-airport transfer tighter if teardown slips. The clinic sends a revised parking map because the staff lot by the therapy entrance will be blocked, and the hotel reconfirms the queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, indoor pool, and fitness room. A later return with a longer connection is available for a modest fare difference, so the remaining question is whether schedule reliability is worth changing the flight.

events.continuity_hook: Opens a personal partner weekend after several work trips, making recovery amenities and total hotel fees more central than flight timing.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the resort, inn, and condo by total cost, beach access, reviews, cancellation terms, room setup, and pool-hot-tub-fitness availability, then decide whether to book Friday through Monday or shorten the stay.
events.scenario_brief: After the Raleigh clinic visit, Kara and her partner begin planning a low-key December beach-and-bike weekend on Amelia Island, driving from Tampa rather than flying. They can leave Friday morning and return Monday, but want enough recovery time built around beach walks, easy cycling, and a quiet final morning before the drive home. A beachfront resort has strong reviews, pool, hot tub, fitness access, coffee makers, and mini-fridges but adds resort and parking fees; a historic-district inn is more walkable for meals but has no pool or hot tub and inconsistent room-fridge details; a condo option has a kitchen and more space but fewer recent reviews and stricter cancellation. The main unresolved choice is whether the beachfront recovery setup is worth the higher total cost and less restaurant walkability.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Amelia Island partner weekend from hotel comparison into booking once the departure day and beachfront resort trade-off settle.
events.interaction_goal: Reserve the refundable resort room with the fee caveat clear, set a Friday drive and grocery-stop plan, outline backup indoor or low-weather activities, and leave the Monday return drive unrushed.
events.scenario_brief: Kara's partner confirms Friday morning departure is workable, and the beachfront resort still has a cancellable room with a queen bed, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness center. The total is higher once parking and the resort fee are included, but it avoids daily driving for beach access and gives them the better post-activity recovery setup. The inn remains cheaper and more walkable for dinners, but the missing hot tub and uncertain fridge make it less appealing for this trip. The remaining planning is around the drive from Tampa, an arrival-day grocery stop, and a weather-flexible Saturday bike route.

events.continuity_hook: Keeps the Amelia Island partner weekend moving after booking, focusing on final logistics rather than reopening the resort-versus-inn decision.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the resort details and fee caveats, decide whether to keep Friday through Monday, set the drive and grocery-stop timing, choose a weather-flexible bike rental plan, and outline backup low-key activities if beach conditions are poor.
events.scenario_brief: A couple of weeks before the Amelia Island weekend, the beachfront resort reconfirms the refundable Friday-to-Monday reservation with a queen room, coffee maker, mini-fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness center, but notes that self-parking has shifted to a gated overflow lot during a small lobby project. The weekend forecast is mixed enough that the Saturday bike plan may need a shorter route or a Sunday swap, and the resort fee still applies even if weather limits beach time. The unresolved pieces are whether to keep the full three-night stay, reserve bikes with a weather-flexible cancellation window, and set a Tampa departure time that avoids arriving too early for check-in.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
versions.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
versions.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
versions.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
versions.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
versions.scope_condition: Flights Kara books for herself for seminars, clinic visits, conferences, or solo positioning legs when she is not coordinating adjacent seats with someone else.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat as a soft default; if true afternoon return departures are unavailable, limited, or unattractive, consider options close to afternoon.
versions.condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return-leg departure time.
versions.default_action: Search for return-flight options departing in the afternoon and present those first when available.
versions.exception_condition: Do not apply as a universal outbound-leg rule; one supporting dialogue separately used a morning outbound while still preferring an afternoon return.
versions.name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
versions.scope_condition: Round-trip itineraries returning to Tampa after work trips, conferences, or partner weekends when the current trip does not specify a different return window.

versions.boundary_condition: This is a soft customer/review-rating default, not an exact 4-star-only rule, not a hotel-class-star requirement, and not a reusable 4.5-star or 3.5-star threshold by itself.
versions.condition: When searching for hotels and a Google rating, review score, or similar customer-facing rating is available, especially for nice, upscale, resort-style, or high-rated stays.
versions.default_action: Filter or rank toward hotels with customer-facing ratings of at least 4.0 stars and report the rating source when known.
versions.exception_condition: If the user specifies a different threshold, prioritizes a budget stay with an explicit lower floor such as 3.5 stars, asks for the cheapest option regardless of quality, only suitable options fall below 4.0, or the rating metric is unclear, follow or clarify the current trip-specific instruction instead of hard-enforcing the 4.0 default.
versions.name: hotel_four_star_customer_rating_floor
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels with clearly good customer-facing ratings, normally at least 4.0 stars, while treating higher ratings such as 4.5 as a bonus and lower stated floors as trip-specific exceptions.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel searches for teaching trips, conferences, clinic visits, and personal stays where customer-facing ratings are available.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat this as a reusable hotel-amenity preference, not a destination, date, price, restaurant/bar, or indoor/outdoor pool preference. Use it as soft unless the current request makes the amenities mandatory.
versions.condition: When selecting or evaluating hotel options.
versions.default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels that offer all three amenities: a pool, a hot tub, and fitness or exercise access; clearly note if one is missing.
versions.exception_condition: If otherwise suitable hotels do not offer all three amenities, present close matches while explicitly noting which of pool, hot tub, or fitness/exercise access is absent.
versions.name: prefer_hotel_pool_hot_tub_fitness
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel choices for multi-night work stays after long teaching days and for active leisure weekends where recovery facilities affect the stay.

versions.boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
versions.condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.
versions.default_action: Filter for or request a queen-size bed when bed type is selectable; if the listing only shows double, twin, or unspecified bedding, confirm the bed setup before booking.
versions.exception_condition: Honor explicit requests for twin beds, multiple separate beds, multiple rooms with different bedding, accessibility-related bedding, or any other trip-specific bed arrangement.
versions.name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
versions.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
versions.scope_condition: Standard hotel rooms for Kara alone or with her partner when no separate-bed arrangement, accessibility bedding need, or alternate setup has been requested.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not generalize this to other amenities such as microwave, balcony, bar, fireplace, room size, location, dates, or price.
versions.condition: When selecting or comparing hotel rooms and in-room amenities are being considered.
versions.default_action: Use an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria, and confirm availability when relevant.
versions.exception_condition: If a hotel otherwise strongly matches the current trip, treat a missing coffee maker or refrigerator/mini-fridge as a point to confirm with the user rather than an automatic rejection.
versions.name: hotel_room_coffee_maker_and_fridge_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefers a hotel room with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
versions.scope_condition: Hotel room comparisons for seminar, clinic-training, and conference stays where she needs an easy morning routine and simple food or drink storage.
